title: EXP-127 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 8: ButtonCheckout Primary StdFormSave on FX_CustomerPortal and a Runtime Cart Walkthrough (Sign In, One Tile Drag to Add To Cart, Cart, Checkout) with an FX_Orders Read-Back
objective: Finish Hello World Part 8 (Phase 8, 21:04-21:50) on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope): set ButtonCheckout's Primary event to the standard Form save event (the tutorial's 'Standard Form Save'; expected StdFormSave) and read it back after a Designer close/reopen; then run the tutorial's runtime walkthrough once: open FX_CustomerPortal in the Web Client, Customer ID FX001 (the FX_ adaptation of the tutorial's 1: FX_Orders customer IDs are FX001/FX002, EXP-073), ButtonSignIn2, drag one item tile onto ButtonAddToCart once, open the cart through the menu Cart button, record the new FX_Orders row, click Checkout once; then close the runtime Form and read FX_Orders back through the FX_Orders Form with one blank query. T1 gate; T2 ButtonCheckout Primary; T3 Designer readback; T4 runtime open and sign-in; T5 drag and cart; T6 Checkout; T7 runtime close, FX_Orders read-back and final audit. Every runtime outcome (including a failed drag or a save error) is a valid observed finding. The sign-in is a UI demonstration, not authentication; this is not a commercial checkout.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109, EXP-111): if a task cannot finish, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T7, for the tab in use (Web Client or Designer; record each tab's own baseline); if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log. A Caption commit that leaves Save disabled is also a stop signal (EXP-110-R2): record it and stop blocked before any further click.

Editing scope: stay in User scope throughout. If an 'Identify Your Editing Scope' dialog appears, confirm it shows User for the signed-in user and accept it unchanged; if it shows any other scope, Cancel it and stop blocked.

Gate (T1, read-only): list the tabs; identify the Web Client (portal app) and Web Designer tabs. Web Client: record which runtime Form (if any) is open and whether it has unsaved changes (if so, record it and stop for the operator); change nothing there. Designer: User scope; FX_CustomerPortal open and clean (Save disabled), no dialog open; if another Form tab is active, select FX_CustomerPortal's tab; if it is not open, open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record: Details > Event Handlers (every group and row; expected as EXP-126 left them: FX_AddToCart rows 0 Collection Make Current object, 1 Collection New object, 2 Generate event FX_SetNewCartEntry( POST() ); FX_SetNewCartEntry SETPROPVALUES(...); FX_CartBtn, FX_HomeBtn, FX_SignInBtn (two rows), FX_SignInBtn2, StdFormPredisplay). Then select ButtonCheckout (FlexLayoutMain cart page region), GridItems and ButtonAddToCart by their Components row Type cell, confirm the Properties header names each, and record: ButtonCheckout Events > Primary (expected blank; if not blank, record it and stop blocked); GridItems Drag From Events and ButtonAddToCart Drop On Events (expected 1 event(s) each). Expanding groups is view only (a group expands on a label double-click); open no ellipsis or list. Verify Save is still disabled. Record each tab's baseline console error count. Screenshots: the Event Handlers tab; ButtonCheckout's Events group.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Property rules (EXP-055, EXP-056, EXP-111, EXP-120): select a component by its Components row (click its Type cell) and confirm the Properties header names it. Lists: open the list with its arrow and click the planned option, then leave the field by clicking a neutral row (never Tab or arrow keys while a list is open); if the planned option is absent, close the list without choosing and stop blocked before any OK or Save. Text fields: click the value cell, one plain fill, one Tab; verify. At most one correction per field. Record the console error count after each action. After each performed step exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK and record it verbatim; any other prompt not covered here: record it, choose the non-changing answer (No or Cancel) and stop blocked. Close every nested dialog you opened with its OK (planned change) or Cancel (no change), innermost first; never leave one open across tasks.

Checkout Primary (T2): select ButtonCheckout by its Components row Type cell and confirm the Properties header; in Events open the Primary list once and record the options near the standard save event; click StdFormSave (the Form's own handlers are listed first, EXP-117; if no option named exactly StdFormSave is offered, record the nearest options, close the list without choosing and stop blocked); leave the field by clicking a neutral row; verify Primary reads StdFormSave; one Designer Save. Screenshots: the Primary list open; the Events group before the Save; the Save response state.

Designer readback (T3, read-only except one close and one reopen): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, and read ButtonCheckout Events > Primary (StdFormSave), the FX_AddToCart and FX_SetNewCartEntry rows, GridItems Drag From Events and ButtonAddToCart Drop On Events. Open no ellipsis, dialog or list. Leave FX_CustomerPortal open and clean. Screenshot: ButtonCheckout's Events group.

Runtime open and sign-in (T4): in the Web Client open FX_CustomerPortal once through the Form menu recent-forms entry if it is listed (close the menu by a second click on its menu-bar button if needed); otherwise through the Web Client Open (Select Form) dialog: clear any leftover filter text (one Control+A, then Backspace; EXP-125), type the Form name key by key in its filter and double-click the exact row (never OK). If neither route finds it, record it and stop blocked. Record any prompt verbatim (answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK; any other prompt: record it, choose No or Cancel and stop blocked). Record the opened Form (title, status bar, visible region: the sign-in page, menu disabled). Click into the Customer ID edit box (EditCustID) once and type FX001 key by key; then click ButtonSignIn2 (the sign-in page's Sign In button, never the left menu's) exactly once; wait for the page to settle (at most 10 seconds) and record: any prompt, the status bar, the console count, the visible region (expected the home page), the GridItems tiles (count; item text of each), the Count edit's value (expected 1), the header Customer ID display (expected FX001) and the menu state. Screenshots: after the sign-in click.

Drag and cart (T5): exactly one drag with the browser drag tool (browser_drag, from the first visible item tile in GridItems to ButtonAddToCart, both by references from the latest snapshot; record which tile). Never use mouse-down/mouse-up or coordinate drags; never repeat the drag, even if nothing visible happens. Wait for the page to settle (at most 10 seconds), then record any prompt or message verbatim (handle as in T4), the console count, the status bar and the visible region. Then click the left menu Cart button once; wait; record the visible region and every GridOrders row (Order Number, Item, Count, Customer ID; whether it is marked new or starred) and the status bar. If GridOrders shows no row, record it and continue to the T5 boundary (no retry). Do not click any row, edit any cell or press any key in T5. Screenshots: after the drag; the cart page.

Checkout (T6): only if T5 recorded a new GridOrders row; otherwise record that T6 was skipped. Click the cart page's Checkout button (ButtonCheckout) exactly once; wait (at most 10 seconds); record any prompt, error or message verbatim (answer an OK-only informational or error message with OK and record it; any other prompt: record it, choose No or Cancel and stop blocked), the console count, the status bar, and GridOrders' rows (whether the new-row mark is gone; the Order Number). Never click Checkout a second time. Screenshot: the cart page after Checkout.

Runtime close, read-back and audit (T7): close the runtime FX_CustomerPortal once through the Web Client Form-close control; if a save prompt appears, record its text and answer No (an unsaved cart row is then discarded; record that). Then open the runtime Form FX_Orders once (the same open route as T4: through the Form menu recent-forms entry if it is listed (close the menu by a second click on its menu-bar button if needed); otherwise through the Web Client Open (Select Form) dialog: clear any leftover filter text (one Control+A, then Backspace; EXP-125), type the Form name key by key in its filter and double-click the exact row (never OK). If neither route finds it, record it and stop blocked); run one query with blank criteria by the EXP-073 route (one Filter in Place click, verify the criteria are blank, then one F4); record every row (Order Number, Customer ID, Item, Count) and the status bar (expected EXP-073's rows 1 FX001 dumbbell 2 and 2 FX002 eggs 1, plus the row saved in T6 if the Checkout saved it). Change nothing; close FX_Orders once (answer No to any save prompt). Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory (ButtonCheckout's Primary; any FX_Orders row created, with its key) and the final state. Screenshots: the FX_Orders rows after the query; the Web Client after the closes.

notes: Part 8 Phase 8 after EXP-126 (Phase 7 accepted 2026-10-23), drafted by the operator assistant from the EXP-126 brief and EXP-125's runtime route. Tutorial mapping: 'Standard Form Save' -> StdFormSave; Customer ID 1 -> FX001, because FX_Orders.FX_CustomerID uses the FX_CustomerID class whose values are FX001/FX002 (EXP-073); the tutorial's bike -> whichever FX_Items tile is first (dumbbell expected). The drag is the only new tool: browser_drag is allowed once (T5); mouse-down/up and coordinate drags stay prohibited. Data: the single Checkout may insert one FX_Orders row in the factory-owned table (as EXP-073 did through the FX_Orders Form); it is recorded for cleanup and not deleted here. A failed drag, an empty cart or a save error is a valid observed finding; the worker records it and does not retry. The read-back through the FX_Orders Form is the separate query the tutorial lacks; it is still UI-level, not a SQL check.
